approved_rules: G1: one concrete falsifiable observation-supported housing-use/demand mechanism is sufficient to continue research; no appreciation proof required; amenity/brand/transit label alone is insufficient.
G2: one credible buyer path is sufficient, including investor-only; budget, task and alternatives still need definition.
G3: unknown is not adverse; material unknown remains a risk, not an automatic pass.
G4: exact selected-unit attributes are tested at G4; cohort averages do not transfer to an individual unit.

summary.source_scope: Targeted public source check for G1 only; no broad regional or all-candidate refresh.

cases.name: Riana South
cases.previous_g1: Education and local working-household demand may support rent; neither university presence nor developer name proves family resale preference.
observed_evidence: UCSI University's official page identifies its active Cheras/Taman Connaught campus and student residential facilities; the page reports a campus population above 15,000.
A property directory places UCSI campus wings and shuttle waiting locations near Riana South, while explicitly leaving route quality unverified.
A 947-sq-ft, 3-bedroom/two-bay rental advertisement is visible, but its move-in date had elapsed; it is not occupancy or collected-rent evidence.
cases.mechanism: Campus-linked students, staff or academic households may rent nearby private three-bedroom stock for access to campus and local daily needs. This is a concrete tenant-use channel to test; it is not a family resale thesis.
cases.interpretation: Pass G1 narrowly because an operating education anchor, nearby advertised residential stock and a rental offer create an observation-supported use pathway. Depth, actual campus-linked tenant share, route quality, rent collection and owner-occupier demand remain unknown.
cases.strongest_falsifier: Fresh verified leasing records show no campus-linked tenants or repeat whole-unit take-up, and direct route inspection shows the stated proximity does not translate into practical access; or visible offers remain stale/unlet after an appropriate observation window.
cases.next_gate: G2 must identify at least one credible buyer path with budget, task and alternatives; do not treat campus users as future owners without evidence.
cases.g3_g4: Not assessed in this replay. Management remains unknown rather than failed; exact unit floor, plan, condition, parking rights and exposure remain G4 checks.

cases.name: PJ Midtown
cases.previous_g1: Section 13 work/service routines may support practical two-bedroom use; no catalyst rent growth credited.
observed_evidence: Developer material identifies PJ Midtown in Section 13 and describes a mixed commercial/residential scheme including offices and retail.
The subject product is a two-bedroom residential unit within this local work/service context.
cases.mechanism: A professional, couple or small household connected to work or services in Section 13 may value a two-bedroom home that reduces routine travel to that local activity cluster. This is a use mechanism to investigate, not proof of actual office occupancy or a rent premium.
cases.interpretation: Pass G1 narrowly: the documented mixed-use environment provides one specific work/service housing task. Actual employer/office occupancy, staff residence, commute paths, leasing and affordability are unmeasured; no rent uplift or appreciation is inferred.
cases.strongest_falsifier: The office/retail component is materially inactive, the target workplaces are not practically reachable from the residence, or comparable renter/buyer evidence shows the 2-bedroom product does not serve those routines.
cases.next_gate: G2 must test one credible buyer path, budget, housing task and alternatives. Existing family/small-household/investor narratives are not yet buyer evidence.
cases.g3_g4: Not assessed in this replay. Governance unknown remains unresolved, not adverse; exact floor, condition, unit rights and parking remain G4 checks.

cases.name: Kelana Mahkota
cases.previous_g1: Lower family-unit quantum may support income economics relative to Sterling; this is a falsifiable hypothesis.
observed_evidence: Current portal pages show advertised 1,260-sq-ft three-bedroom rentals, including an approximate RM2,300-RM2,500/month cluster; repeated similar rows may be duplicates and are counted once as asking evidence.
Portal pages identify a local daily-service context including grocery/retail, school, healthcare and local bus options; routes and practical access have not been ground-checked.

A portal's 'SS7 station' / 'upcoming rail link' claim is ambiguous. Official Rapid Bus material identifies a Taman Bahagia–SS6/SS7 Rapid On-Demand service area; no rail-access claim is used in this G1 pass.
cases.mechanism: A local household needing a conventional three-bedroom home may use Kelana Jaya's everyday service network and project-scale residential facilities, while rental listings show this family-sized product is marketed to tenants. This is a household-use path to test, separate from any rail/TOD story.
cases.interpretation: Pass G1 narrowly because the product/use match and marketed rental channel are observable, and local routine services are reported. The evidence does not establish absorption, collected rent, family buyer willingness, walkability or rail proximity; duplicate ads are not independent demand.
cases.strongest_falsifier: The rental rows prove to be duplicated/stale or partition-dependent, conventional whole-unit take-up is not verified, and on-site route checks show daily household services are not practically accessible; or the target household task is better met by materially cheaper alternatives.
cases.next_gate: G2 must establish one credible buyer path and compare budget, housing task and alternatives. For investor path, G5/G6 later test price and exit; no income advantage over Sterling is passed here.
cases.g3_g4: Not assessed in this replay. Management remains unknown rather than failed; exact selected-unit plan, floor, condition, exposure, bay rights and circulation remain G4 checks.
